paper.authors: X.-Y. Li, J. Wang, Z.-T. Wen
paper.title: Representation of finite-order solutions to linear differential equations with exponential-sum coefficients

scope: The seven numbered main results, supplementary Lemma 5.2 prime, and complete conclusions of Examples 3.8 and 3.9. Unrelated CRG Theorem 1.1 is in its separate project.

entries.alignment: Literal row·Q·M·P polynomial operator equals the shifted Euler operator; equivalence with the actual ODE for exp(a*z)*u(exp z), including entirety and finite order. Q uses falling factorials, M uses Stirling numbers of the second kind.
entries.qualification: A fixed unnormalized exponent need not be an indicial root. Root conclusion uses u(0) != 0, obtained by absorbing the zero order of a nonzero u into the exponent.

entries.alignment: From the monic actual ODE and entire finite-order f, constructs indicial-root exponents, polynomial u, polynomial factors F of degree p, and sum K <= n. C=1 and F=X^p suffice. Roots and degree budget are conclusions.
entries.qualification: The displayed existential representation is covered by the explicit choices C_j=1 and F_j,p=X^p; no extra restriction on the input solution is imposed. Exact coupled triangular equations for block coefficients are proved separately.

entries.alignment: Nontrivial finite-order entire solution exists iff a normalized polynomial solution of the literal matrix equation exists, with an indicial-root exponent.
The polynomial identity in the exponent implies an actual nonzero entire finite-order pure exponential solution. The paper nonzero-exponent case is included.
Every natural leading power gamma and every nonzero complex common frequency; actual iterated derivatives and ODE. Finite order iff a finite sum of polynomial factors times linear exponentials.
entries.paper_supplement: Section 5.4, p.130: finite exponential upper bound suffices. Remove the lowest appearing exponential factor before using the endpoint root bound. Work in the finite-order translation-invariant solution space so all Floquet components retain finite order.

entries.alignment: Actual nonpolynomial entire finite-order monic solution has order exactly one and finite positive type. Direct proof establishes two-sided genuine central-index bounds; recurrence proof establishes representation before growth.

Entire coefficients composed with exp and nonzero polynomial factors with strictly increasing degrees; mean type of the whole sum implies every entire coefficient is a polynomial. A stronger entry assumes only a global exponential bound on the whole sum; cancellation is allowed.

From nonzero polynomial factors of strictly increasing degrees, coefficient functions holomorphic on C minus zero, and one global exponential bound for the whole sum, derives a finite Laurent representation for each coefficient on every nonzero w, with the literal symmetric integer range [-N,N]. The named-sum wrapper accepts g and its representation. Holomorphy at zero yields an ordinary polynomial on all of C.
entries.qualification: No individual coefficient bound, finite Fourier support, Laurent representation, or holomorphy at zero is assumed for the Laurent conclusion. The value at zero is unconstrained until the holomorphic-at-zero corollary. Entirety of g is derivable from the coefficient hypotheses, so a separate entirety hypothesis is unnecessary.
entries.proof: Polynomial-periodic coefficient extraction; proved periodic Fourier tail vanishing and reconstruction; evaluate at log w and use exp(log w)=w; pad finite support by zeros to a symmetric integer interval.

entries.verified_conclusion: Every entire finite-order solution is exactly exp(z)*(A+B*z); every such function is an entire finite-order solution; exp(z) and z*exp(z) are linearly independent. The classification is derived without invoking Frei.
Every nonzero entire solution of f''+f'+exp(z)*f=0 fails FiniteOrder. The polynomial top-coefficient obstruction and the normalized polynomial extraction are proved.
